newsitem.title: UK: British jobless rate drops to 5.5 percent in July.
newsitem.headline: British jobless rate drops to 5.5 percent in July.

text.p: Unemployment in Britain fell by 49,800 in July, pulling the jobless rate down to 5.5 percent from 5.7 percent in June, official figures showed on Wednesday.
The Office for National Statistics also said growth in average earnings, an important barometer of future inflationary trends, remained steady in June at 4.25 percent.
The drop in the jobless rate took the total number of unemployed to 1.55 million, the lowest level seen since September 1980.
The fall in the number of people out of work was higher than expected. Bank economists had predicted a decline of 31,000.
The strong fall in the jobless rate indicates a strengthening economy but the steady earnings growth would suggest that inflationary pressures might be in check, analysts said.

"It (the fall in unemployment) is bigger than expected and does indicate strength in the economy but underlying average earnings are unchanged...As long as there is an absence of wage pressure...the extent to which unemployment is falling is not going to be of concern to the markets," said John Shepperd with Yamaichi International
